title: The current Concord group
summary: He introduces Fatali, Rossi, Richards and earlier pianist Delores Leacock.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Pete Morgan. And who are the other members of your group now?
Well, on bass, Doug Richards. Piano is Joe Fatali. Clarinet is Sonny Rossi. (Inaudible).
Right. And, what do you, I mean, what could you tell us about the other members of hte group?
Joe Fatali, he's been with me since last January. I had a girl pianist before then, Delores Leacock. She's from

Panama. She got ill last December. She had been with me here 10 years. Yeah. She got one of those nervous things. So, she had to stop for awhile. So, she went back home to take care of herself. You know, with her parents.
And then I brought Joe Fatali in. So, he's a very, very nice slow pianist, good jazzman. He stayed in Brooklyn for years. But, he's been up here for years now. Brooklyn, I think, was his home.

Sonny Rossi. He's been up here. He used to have a band here years ago like, I don't know if it was the 30's or the 40's. He was the drummer in his own band. He had a Latin band, and played in the Imperial Room. And, he went away after so many years. He wasn't here when I first came. He went to California.
So, when I came in '67, then he came back up here about, I don't know, maybe the 70's. He joined, he's been with me now about 4 years, 3, going on 4 years.

clarinet. But, he was a good clarinet, but he's a good writer. He writes, too. His son plays very good, son plays very good piano. His son sat in when the young lady that was playing with me got sick until I got Joe Fatali. He's going to school up in New Brunswick. Right. Somewhere. I don't know. Up near Syracuse somewhere.
Oh, no. New Paltz? Not New Brunswick? What's upstate? [Binghamton?]

Well, as I was saying, it's near Syracuse. So, he came down and played piano with me over the weekends until I got Joe Fatali. And, he was very good. He's gonna be a doctor, too, and take his music. And Doug Richards, he took Jimmy Stiles' place. Jimmy Stiles was the bass player when I first came in. He's back in New York. He was up here for about 12 years. Jimmy Stiles was. Doug's been with me now two or a little better. A good bass player. And, I think that's the group that I have now. They're all very nice guys. I'll

call them up. I'll say yeah, I'll make the 5:00. You know, if I got a 5:00 in the lounge? I just tell them. They say yeah, I'll make it. I'll see you on the next set. They're right there to do the job. [Phone Interruption]
